---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Tutorial: one undercut, beside one rebuttal"
description: "Four lines and the whole distinction the format exists for. A step concludes that the suspect broke in. One objection denies the conclusion outright and would be just as good an objection if the step had never been written: that is a rebuttal. The other objection grants everything the step's premise says and denies that it carries, by taking the step itself as a premise: that is an undercut. The syntax difference is one conjunct, `AND $prints-ev`, and deleting it silently turns the undercut into a rebuttal with no diagnostic anywhere. The two also behave differently in the solve, and the file says how."
---

# ===========================================================================
# THE SCHEMA, exactly:
#
#     rebuttal   $r  q ~@claim | @grounds
#     undercut   $u  q ~@claim | @grounds AND $target
#
# The `AND $target` conjunct IS the undercut. It is the only thing that
# makes the line an attack on the inference rather than on the conclusion,
# and it is one token long, which is why this is the most common first-pass
# structural error in the corpus.
#
# WHY THE TARGET GOES ON THE PREMISE SIDE, since it looks backwards.
# `~$id` is banned by the lint (error E3): an evidence is not a proposition
# and there is nothing to negate. What the format offers instead is exactly
# the reading an undercut wants, "granted that the step is in force, here is
# why it nonetheless fails to carry", and that is a condition, so it lives
# to the right of the given bar.
#
# THE QUESTION TO ASK OF EVERY OBJECTION, before writing a line:
#
#     Does this objection grant the premise and deny the connection,
#     or does it deny the conclusion whatever the premise says?
#
# Grants and denies the connection: undercut. Denies the conclusion: rebuttal.
# ===========================================================================

@prints [The suspect's prints are on the inside of the window frame] 0.9:
@guilty [The suspect broke in on the night of the theft]:  # check: 0.6
$prints-ev [prints inside the frame put a hand on the window] 0.8 @guilty | @prints: the step under attack from two directions below

# ---- the rebuttal: denies the conclusion ----------------------------------
# @alibi says nothing about the prints. It would be exactly as good an
# objection in a version of this map where the prints were never mentioned,
# and that is the mark of a rebuttal: it is aimed at the claim, not at the
# reasoning.

@alibi [The suspect is on a bus camera across town at the time] 0.5:
$rebut [being somewhere else is being somewhere else] 0.85 ~@guilty | @alibi:

# ---- the undercut: grants the premise, denies that it carries -------------
# @visited grants the prints completely. It even needs them: the objection
# only makes sense as an alternative explanation OF the prints. What it
# denies is that prints on a frame get you from there to a break-in.
#
# DROP THE `AND $prints-ev` AND THIS BECOMES A MERE REBUTTAL. The line would
# still parse, still render, still solve, and would then be claiming that an
# earlier invited visit is direct evidence of innocence, which is not what
# anybody meant.

@visited [The suspect was invited into the studio a week earlier] 0.6:
$uc [an invited visit leaves the same prints] 0.7 ~@guilty | @visited AND $prints-ev:

# ---- how they differ in the solve -----------------------------------------
# Solved 2026-08-04 (D36 defaults, solve_map.py):
#   @prints 0.893   @alibi 0.497   @visited 0.601
#   @guilty check 0.60 -> 0.440
#   $prints-ev 0.80 -> 0.794     $rebut 0.85 -> 0.835     $uc 0.70 -> 0.699
#
# Note the shape of $uc's own readout: one row, P(U), not the two slab rows
# every other line gets. That is the compile telling you what it is. An
# undercut is a switch on another line, so there is no premise slab of its
# own for the symmetric floor to mirror across.
#
# The two attacks do different work, and the difference is not a matter of
# degree.
#
# A rebuttal carries a floor of its own: it pushes ~@guilty up directly, and
# it would do that even if $prints-ev were deleted from the file.
#
# An undercut carries NO floor of its own. It compiles as a pure inhibitor
# of its target, so the negated conclusion it names gets no independent push
# from it (SOLVER_SEMANTICS 1.2, the factored-A compile). Two consequences
# that surprise people, both measured elsewhere in the corpus: an undercut
# whose target has no strength at all moves nothing whatsoever, and an
# undercut of a rebuttal reinstates the claim only towards where it would
# have been with the rebuttal absent, never past it.
#
# The authoring consequence, and it is easy to miss: if the source also
# asserts the FACT the objection rests on, and you want that fact to bear on
# the conclusion in its own right, the undercut cannot carry it. Write the
# fact as an ordinary evidence line beside the undercut. The two do not
# double-count, because the inhibitor acts on the inference and the plain
# line acts on the claim.
#
# Next: t5-double-undercut, which answers this undercut without writing `~$`.
